IAttributeSystem gen-ed / NUPath

"Attributes" is the generic name for what NU calls NUPath, and what other schools call gen-ed, distribution requirements, or learning outcomes. The grad panel grid, course chips, and PDF export all read from this port. Leave gridCodes empty and the grid disappears entirely.

Port key
"attributeSystem"
Consumed by
GradPanel (grid), Header (coverage badge), CourseCard (attribute chips), PDF export (labels), specialTermUtils (computeGrantedAttrs feeds here)
Override when
Your institution has a codified gen-ed or distribution requirement framework

Contract

All members are getter methods, not properties.

MethodReturnsPurpose
getSystemName()stringDisplay name shown as the grad panel section title. e.g. "NUPath", "Gen Ed", "GIRs". Empty string → attribute grid is hidden.
getAttributes()Attribute[]Full list of attribute definitions including legacy codes that exist in course data but are no longer active requirements.
getGridLayout()string[][]2-D array of attribute codes for the grad panel grid, e.g. [["ND","EI","IC","FQ"], ...]. Excludes legacy-only codes. Row × column order is display order.
getGridCodes()string[]Flat ordered list from getGridLayout().flat(). Source of truth for grid rendering and the coverage progress badge.
getLabel(code)stringReturns the display label for an attribute code. Covers all codes including legacy ones. Falls back to the code itself if no label found.
canDoubleDip()booleanWhether a course can simultaneously satisfy an attribute and a major/minor requirement. Returns true at most institutions (including NU).
getMaxPerAttribute()number|nullMaximum courses that can satisfy any single attribute. null = unlimited (most schools).
getCoverage(placements, courseMap, grantedCodes?)Set<string>Returns set of covered attribute codes. See below.

getCoverage() signature

getCoverage(
  placements:   { [courseId: string]: semId: string },  // courses in the plan
  courseMap:    { [courseId: string]: Course },          // full course objects
  grantedAttrs: Set<string>                             // from computeGrantedAttrs()
): Set<string>

grantedAttrs is optional (defaults to empty Set). Compute it with computeGrantedAttrs(specialTermPl, types) before calling getCoverage. This is how a placed co-op causes the EX cell to turn green — no hardcoded "EX" in the attribute system itself.

// Standard usage in GradPanel, Header
import { computeGrantedAttrs } from "../core/specialTermUtils.js";

const grantedAttrs = computeGrantedAttrs(specialTermPl, specialTerms?.types);
const npCovered    = attributeSystem.getCoverage(placements, courseMap, grantedAttrs);

Attribute typedef

FieldTypeNotes
codestringShort code used in course data and as the grid cell key, e.g. "ND", "EX".
labelstringDisplay name shown in the grid cell and tooltips.
descriptionstring?Optional longer description for an info panel or tooltip. Not currently rendered.

Northeastern — NUPath

13 attributes. 12 in the 3×4 grid. 1 legacy code (WF) in labels only — present in old course data and needed for PDF export but no longer displayed as an active requirement.

Grid layout (3×4, 12 codes)

NDEIICFQ
SIADDDER
WDWIEXCE

Labels (13 entries, includes WF)

NDNatural/Designed World
EICreative Express/Innov
ICInterpreting Culture
FQFormal/Quant Reasoning
SISocieties/Institutions
ADAnalyzing/Using Data
DDDifference/Diversity
EREthical Reasoning
WF1st Yr Writing (legacy)
WDAdv Writing Disc
WIWriting Intensive
EXIntegration Experience
CECapstone Experience

systemName: "NUPath". getCoverage iterates course.attributes for all placed courses, then adds every code from grantedAttrs.

Legacy code handling: WF appears in course data from before ~2018. It is in attributes and labels so PDF export resolves the label correctly, but it is not in gridLayout or gridCodes, so the grad panel never shows it as a requirement to satisfy.

Generic default

// src/adapters/generic/attributeSystem.js
export default {
  getSystemName()       { return ""; },      // no section title → grid hidden
  getAttributes()       { return []; },
  getGridLayout()       { return []; },
  getGridCodes()        { return []; },
  getLabel(code)        { return code; },   // fall back to raw code
  canDoubleDip()        { return true; },
  getMaxPerAttribute()  { return null; },
  getCoverage()         { return new Set(); },
};

With an empty getGridCodes(), the GradPanel hides the attribute grid entirely. No errors, no empty boxes.

Implementing for your institution

  1. Define your attribute codes as { code, label } objects in the attributes array.
  2. Build gridLayout as a 2-D array — each inner array is one row of the grid. Arrange codes in the display order you want.
  3. Derive gridCodes = gridLayout.flat().
  4. Derive labels = Object.fromEntries(attributes.map(a => [a.code, a.label])). Add any legacy codes manually if they appear in your course data.
  5. Implement getCoverage: iterate placed courses, union their attributes arrays, add grantedAttrs.
  6. Set systemName to your framework's display name.
✦
Course objects use the generic field name attributes. Your course JSON should include an attributes array with the short codes, e.g. "attributes": ["ND", "FQ"]. The NU scraper writes this field as nuPath in catalog data, which the adapter normalizes to attributes when loading.
